message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States:

| Airport | City | State | IATA Code | Notable Features |
|---------|------|-------|-----------|------------------|
| Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport | Atlanta | Georgia | ATL | Largest passenger airport in the world by enplanements; major hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| Los Angeles International Airport | Los Angeles | California | LAX | Major gateway to Asia and the Pacific; busiest airport on the West Coast. |
| Chicago O’Hare International Airport | Chicago | Illinois | ORD | One of the busiest airports in the world; major hub for United Airlines and American Airlines. |
| Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport | Dallas/Fort Worth | Texas | DFW | One of the largest airports by land area; major hub for American Airlines. |
| Denver International Airport | Denver | Colorado | DEN | Largest airport by land area in the U.S.; major hub for United Airlines and Southwest Airlines. |
| John F. Kennedy International Airport | New York City | New York | JFK | Major international gateway; hub for many airlines including Delta and JetBlue. |
| San Francisco International Airport | San Francisco | California | SFO | Major hub for United Airlines; key gateway to Asia and the Pacific Rim. |
| Seattle–Tacoma International Airport | Seattle | Washington | SEA | Major hub for Alaska Airlines and a growing hub for Delta. |
| Miami International Airport | Miami | Florida | MIA | Major hub for American Airlines; key gateway to Latin America and the Caribbean. |
| Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport | Phoenix | Arizona | PHX | Major hub for American Airlines; one of the busiest airports in the Southwest. |

These airports are among the busiest in terms of passenger traffic and serve as major hubs for both domestic and international flights.
message.reasoning: The user asks for major airports in the US. This is a straightforward request for information. No tool needed.
